modules.description: The right mental model for working with AI. What AI is good at, where it falls short, and how to think about prompting — before you build anything.

lessons.content: AI — artificial intelligence — is software that can understand language, answer questions, and generate content. The AI tools you'll use in this course are conversational: you type something, and they respond. That's it. No coding, no configuration, no special syntax. Just type what you need, the same way you'd message a colleague.
lessons.title: What AI Actually Is (No Jargon)

activities.title: The Mental Model: AI as a Capable Assistant

lessons.content:
The best way to think about AI is as a very capable assistant who needs direction. It's not going to replace you — it doesn't know your company, your context, your judgment. But it can do a lot of the heavy lifting: research, writing, analysis, formatting, brainstorming, checking work, and building things.

Your job is to direct it. AI's job is to do the work — fast.

| You Bring | AI Brings |
|---|---|
| Context about your company and situation | Broad knowledge across topics |
| Professional judgment and decision-making | Speed — it works in seconds |
| Knowledge of what "good" looks like | Tireless patience — it never gets annoyed |
| Accountability for the output | Ability to draft, rewrite, and iterate instantly |
lessons.title: The Mental Model: AI as a Capable Assistant

lessons.content:
AI gets you 80% of the way there — fast. Your expertise finishes the job.

This is the pattern you'll see over and over throughout this course:
- AI drafts, you refine
- AI researches, you verify
- AI builds, you review

The combination is what makes it powerful.
lessons.title: The 80/20 Rule

activities.title: What AI Is Good At vs. What It's Bad At

lessons.content:
**AI is good at:**
- Explaining concepts clearly at whatever level you need
- Drafting written content (emails, memos, reports, summaries)
- Analyzing data, documents, and spreadsheets
- Following instructions and repeating processes consistently
- Brainstorming ideas and alternatives
- Building simple tools, templates, and automations

**AI is not good at:**
- Knowing your company's specific context (unless you tell it)
- Making judgment calls that require human experience
- Guaranteeing 100% accuracy on specific facts or numbers
- Replacing the need for professional expertise on critical matters
- Accessing your internal systems (unless connected via tools)
lessons.title: What AI Is Good At vs. What It's Bad At

lessons.content:
"Prompting" sounds technical, but it's just clear communication. When you give AI a prompt, you're telling it what you want — like giving instructions to a colleague. The clearer your instructions, the better the result.

You don't need special formulas or templates. Just be specific:

- **Vague:** "Help me with revenue recognition" → You'll get a generic overview
- **Specific:** "I need to evaluate a software contract with multiple deliverables under ASC 606. Walk me through how to apply the five-step model to this scenario." → You'll get exactly what you need

You'll get better at this naturally as you practice. That's what the rest of this course is for.
lessons.title: How to Think About Prompting

modules.description: Hands-on steps. Set up your accounts, create your training portfolio organization, and build your first agent.

lessons.content:
If you haven't already, create free accounts on the AI platforms you'll be using. You need at least one of the big three — pick whichever you prefer, or try all of them.

- **ChatGPT** → https://chat.openai.com
- **Claude** → https://claude.ai
- **Grok** → https://grok.com

You'll also need an account on **My AI For One** for your training portfolio:

- **My AI For One** → https://myaifor.one
lessons.title: Step 1: Create Your Free Accounts

activities.title: Step 2: Create Your Training Portfolio Organization

lessons.content:
Go to **My AI For One** (https://myaifor.one) and sign in.

Create a new **organization** called:

> **My Training Portfolio**

This organization is your personal AI workspace for this course. Every agent you build, every artifact you create — it all lives here. Think of it as your training folder, except instead of static files, it holds working AI agents.

> **Already have one?** If you created this organization in a previous session, you're good. Just make sure you can access it.
lessons.title: Step 2: Create Your Training Portfolio Organization

activities.title: Step 3: Create Your Using AI Series Agent

lessons.content:
Now you're going to create your first agent. This is the home base for everything you'll build in the **Using AI** training series.

1. In **My AI For One**, navigate to **HUB**
2. Make sure you're inside your **My Training Portfolio** organization
3. Click **Create Agent**
4. **Name:** `Using AI Series Agent`
5. **Instructions:** Paste the following:

```
You are my portfolio agent for the "Using AI" training series. Your role is to help me track, organize, and build on everything I learn and create throughout this course.

You know about the following modules and what I'm building in each:
- Module 1: Gaining Knowledge — research agent for learning topics deeply
- Module 2: Communication — communications agent for writing and messaging
- Module 3: Analysis & Review — review agent for validating and checking work
- Module 4: Improving Manual Tasks — automation agent for streamlining workflows
- Module 5: Building Tools & Dashboards — custom tools and applications

As I complete each module, I'll tell you what I built and what I learned. Help me:
- Keep track of the agents and artifacts I've created
- Suggest ways to connect what I've learned across modules
- Help me reflect on how I'm applying AI in my actual work
- Remind me of tools, prompts, and techniques from earlier modules when they're relevant

You are practical and direct. You work with me in the context of a finance function — accounting, FP&A, tax, treasury, audit, or whatever area I work in. Keep things grounded in real work, not theory.
```

6. **Save** the agent.
lessons.title: Step 3: Create Your Using AI Series Agent

lessons.content:
Open a conversation with your new **Using AI Series Agent** and send it a quick message:

> "I just set up my training portfolio. I'm about to start Module 1 — Using AI to Gain Knowledge. What should I keep in mind?"

Read its response. This is your portfolio agent — it's going to grow with you as you move through the course.
lessons.title: Step 4: Test Your Agent

activities.title: Step 5: Quick Test of an AI Platform

lessons.content:
Before moving to Module 1, take two minutes to make sure your AI tool is working. Go to ChatGPT, Claude, or Grok and ask it something simple:

> "What's the difference between accrual accounting and cash accounting?"

Or ask about literally anything — sports, cooking, history, whatever. The point is: you type, it responds. That's the interface. No setup, no configuration. You're ready.
lessons.title: Step 5: Quick Test of an AI Platform

modules.description: How the setup and mental model from this module apply every time you start something new with AI.

activities.title: Starting a New Project at Work

lessons.content:
Before diving into any new work project, think about what AI can help with and set up the right tools. Just like you'd set up a project folder, you can set up a project agent — one that already knows the context, the goal, and how you want to work.

This applies to audits, close cycles, implementations, budgets, or anything else with a defined scope.
lessons.title: Starting a New Project at Work

lessons.content:
Share the mental model from this module — AI as an assistant that needs direction — to help colleagues start using AI productively without overthinking it.

The most common mistake new users make is either expecting too much (AI as magic) or too little (AI as a search engine). This module's framing fixes both.
lessons.title: Onboarding a New Team Member

lessons.content:
When your company evaluates new AI tools or platforms, you'll have a practical framework for assessing them: what are they good at, where does human judgment still apply, and how do they fit into your existing workflow?

The "AI as capable assistant" model applies regardless of which tool you're evaluating.
lessons.title: Evaluating AI Tools

lessons.content:
Your training portfolio is the beginning of your personal AI practice. As you build more agents and tools throughout this course, you're developing a library of reusable AI assets that make you more effective over time.

Think of each module not just as a lesson, but as a contribution to something you'll actually use after the course is done.
lessons.title: Building an AI Practice

activities.title: No Bonus for Module 0 — Just Get Started

lessons.content:
Module 0 is your foundation — there's no optional deep-dive here. The only goal is to have your accounts set up, your training portfolio created, and your Using AI Series Agent ready to go.

Starting with Module 1, every module will have a Bonus section where you can build a dedicated specialist agent and add it to your portfolio. By the end of the course, you'll have five working agents.

For now: you're set up. Move on to Module 1.
lessons.title: No Bonus for Module 0 — Just Get Started

modules.description: Key terms introduced in this module, explained in plain language.

lessons.content: Software that can understand language, answer questions, and generate content. In this course, we're using AI tools that you interact with by typing — like having a conversation with a very knowledgeable assistant.
lessons.title: AI (Artificial Intelligence)

lessons.content: The technology behind tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok. It's trained on vast amounts of text and learns to understand and generate language. You don't need to know how it works — just know that it's what powers the tools you're using.
lessons.title: LLM (Large Language Model)

lessons.content: The question or instruction you type into an AI tool. "Prompting" is simply the act of telling AI what you want — like giving clear direction to an assistant. The clearer your prompt, the better the response.
lessons.title: Prompt

lessons.content: A reusable AI setup where you've given the AI specific instructions about its role and expertise. Instead of starting fresh each time, you come back to this agent and it already knows its job. Your Using AI Series Agent is your first one.
lessons.title: Agent

lessons.content: A workspace in My AI For One that groups your agents and projects together. Your "My Training Portfolio" organization is where all your training work lives.
lessons.title: Organization

lessons.content: The collection of agents, tools, and artifacts you build throughout this course. It's tangible proof of what you can do with AI — not just a certificate, but working assets you can use in your job starting tomorrow.
